title: SPF basics
caption: SPF measures how much longer a sunscreen lets you stay in UV light before your skin starts to redden — but that number was tested in a lab at 2mg per cm², roughly twice the amount most people actually apply. In Dubai's summer, that gap matters more than elsewhere: UV index regularly hits 11+ between May and September, and you're cycling between direct sun and air-conditioned interiors all day, which makes reapplication easy to forget. SPF also only measures UVB protection. UVA rays — the ones that drive pigmentation and accelerate skin aging — require a separate claim: look for 'broad spectrum', 'PA+++', or a UVA circle logo on the label. Mineral sunscreens (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) scatter both UV types and tend to sit better on darker skin tones without leaving a pronounced white cast in newer formulations. Chemical filters absorb UV and can feel lighter, but some require 20 minutes to activate after application. Neither is universally better — the one you'll apply consistently, and reapply every two hours, is the right one. Not medical advice, just the honest basics.
